headline: Margin gains erased by taxes and lapped one-off gains
summary_short: GlobalFoundries' Q1 2026 revenue rose 3.1% y/y to $1,634M on higher wafer shipments and Technology Services growth, with gross margin up 520bps to 27.6%, but net income fell 51% y/y to $103M as income tax expense jumped $97M and Q1 2025's one-time JV step-acquisition gain didn't repeat.
summary_long: Revenue grew 3.1% y/y to $1,634M (down 10.7% q/q, seasonally) on 6.6% higher wafer shipments and 11.2% Technology Services growth, offset by lower average selling prices. Gross margin expanded 520bps to 27.6% on favorable mix and lower D&A. SG&A rose 80.5% on lower tool-sale gains and acquisition headcount costs. Net income fell 51% y/y to $103M despite higher operating income, as income tax expense rose $97M (43.8% effective rate) on German deferred-tax timing, and Q1 2025's $31M JV step-acquisition gain did not repeat. Operating cash flow rose to $542M; capex was $312M; GF repurchased $400M of shares (including a $300M Mubadala block) under a new $500M authorization. No forward guidance was disclosed in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Grew 3.1% y/y on 6.6% higher wafer shipment volumes (579k, 300mm-equivalent) and 11.2% growth in Technology Services (mask/reticle revenue), partly offset by lower average selling prices in some end markets.

Gross margin expanded 520bps to 27.6% (from 22.4%) on favorable Manufacturing Services revenue mix and $52M lower depreciation and amortization, partly offset by lower customer underutilization payments.

The 27% y/y gross-profit gain outpaced opex growth (SG&A +80.5%, R&D +3.9%), lifting operating income 19% y/y; the q/q decline from Q4 2025 is not explained in the release, which discusses only y/y comparisons.
Roughly flat-to-down y/y (-2.4%) as the gross-profit gain and lower D&A were offset by higher SG&A; the 33% q/q sequential decline from Q4 2025 is not explained in the release.

Fell 51% y/y to $103M despite higher operating income: income tax expense rose $97M (43.8% effective rate vs -8.2% in Q1 2025) on German deferred-tax-asset timing, and Q1 2025's $31M gain from a joint-venture step-acquisition plus $6M higher fair-value gains did not repeat.
Tracks the 51% y/y decline in net income; diluted share count was little changed, so the per-share drop mirrors the net-income drop.

Operating cash flow rose to $542M on higher non-cash items and working capital; capex rose to $312M on facility investment; GF repurchased $400M of shares (a $300M Mubadala block plus $100M open-market) under a new $500M authorization.
